summary: ```# Marvelous Designer: Learning Day - Hat Making Collection p04 Pure Enjoyment Version 3 - Baseball Cap ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will create a baseball cap in Marvelous Designer. The process involves importing background images, creating various components of the cap, and adjusting the design to fit a virtual model. ## Importing the Background Before starting to make the baseball cap, we first import the background picture. Insert the background picture into the Marvelous Designer 2D window. After that, you can see that its proportion is relatively large. ## Setting Image Size We set the size here to 50% and confirm. It can be compared that its size is still a little big, so we change it to 30%. Then use the internal line tool to create the effect on the picture. When we create half of it, we can finish this version. After completion, select to open and begin to draw other parts of the version. ## Creating the Hat Body In the process of drawing, press the Ctrl key. Click to start and create a red curve point. If you want to create a straight line, just press the left button. Remember to release the Ctrl key. After drawing the baseball cap, we first create the body of the hat. To create the body, we will use the middle shape first. ### Joint Version After choosing this shape, create a joint version. Note that it is to create a joint version. When we create a joint version, if we modify any of the versions, other outer frame light green versions that are linked to each other will be modified together. After creating a total of six versions, we are going to start to sew the version. ## Sewing the Hat You can't use this version at the moment, so let's turn it over first. The method of sewing is very simple; we use the line sewing tool to sew the two sides together. After sewing, we put it in 3D space to adjust its arrangement, and then open the animation. ### Simulating the Hat Then we start to simulate. Because the gravity is off, we can apply a hard drive to all the sheets. After holding up, we can see that it's like the half of a basketball. That's the basis of the baseball cap we often talk about. To prevent it from deforming, we also change its physical attribute to the attribute of Fograin Leather here. ## Adjusting the Cap Since this attribute is relatively hard, we can remove the hardening if we connect it. Direct simulation is also OK. Then we select all the panels without opening the simulation and drag them to the head of the virtual model. After opening the simulation, let it be covered on the head of the virtual model. ### Fitting the Cap Here, because I used the virtual model prepared before, we can reduce the surface strength of the virtual model to 0, making the panel closer to the head. If you want to modify the head of the hat or make it fit the model's head shape, first, we can lengthen the entire panel in the vertical direction. ## Modifying the Panel When we lengthen the entire panel, the height of the hat as a whole will be increased, and it will be a little longer. But it does not widen the entire height of the hat in the head. If we want to widen it, we need to select the center of the panel, double-click to use the center point, and then widen our selection. ### Final Adjustments We can drag the panel in the state of opening the simulation so that it fits the head of our virtual model. By doing this, we can quickly double-click the panel to open the simulation. After that, you can add the results here. ## Creating the Face After the adjustment, we are going to start making the face. Let's find the two panels of the forehead first. For other panels, we can freeze them for the time being. Then select the middle to open the line, select the symmetry to open the border. In this way, when we modify one side of it, the other side will also be modified at the same time. ### Positioning the Panels Because the previous version was re-activated, now we can re-arrange the position of this version. After activation, use the positioning ball tool to adjust it to the position we want to sew. Then we can start to create a sewing line. We use the free sewing tool to sew a long section first, then press the Shift key. ## Sewing the Lines From the point in front of us to the right side to sew, the length that comes out is the same. We press the Shift key; don't sew it on the side next to the back. Here is the same; sew from right to left. If you turn to the back of the board, it will still start from this point, from right to left. ### Editing the Sewing Line Just like when we did the dress cap before, it was the same. Here, because the bend strength of the board is relatively large, it will be connected into one. Then we need to use the editing sewing line tool to select all the sewing lines and set its folding angle at the bottom. ## Finalizing the Design Here we set it to 270 degrees, which is an opposite fold angle. But when we set the right angle, we will find that this board can't be turned over no matter what. In fact, it can be compared, as an example, it is a little too wide. So we can adjust the width of this board first to fit the width of the board in front of us. ### Cutting and Adjusting Because I want to use the front of these two boards as a reference, we can cut points according to the sewing line. After selecting this set of sewing lines with the editing sewing line, there is an increase point at the end of the right key. Because each section is the next starting point, you actually choose to be in the ending position or starting position; it will turn into a breakpoint. ## Using the Multi-layer Tool After forming a breakpoint, we can use this point as a basis to adjust. So from this point on, use the built-in multi-layer tool to click and draw a split line. After roughly drawing, use the edit board tool to select this line and cut it off. The rest of the parts can be deleted by clicking. ### Simulation Effects After we turn on the simulation, we will find that it is not like before; it will have such a curved effect. Then we can make it a little longer according to the need, letting it be closer to the hat in real life. Or you can change its curve. ## Refining Details In order to better reference the effect, we can first reduce the particle distance and the conflict thickness of these now activated boards. Let's adjust the curve a bit, then we can also make the curve a bit rounder. The feature of the double-edged hat is that sometimes we can see the sewing line from the outside. ### Creating Fake Sewing Lines Here we use the line section to click along this side. You can create a fake sewing line along this side. If you want to modify the type of sewing line, first, we can change the name of the window on the side to Top Stitch. Then adjust its properties in the attribute editor below. ## Crafting the Support Structure Regarding the sewing line, first, we can choose whether it is a three-dimensional OBJ file or Texture. Then we can change the border. The border is the line between this sewing line to the section we choose. In real life, these hats are supported by a part of the stock price. ### Internal Structure Then we can also make this effect in the software. Because now the hat is close to the forehead, so we first reverse-activate the virtual model. After finishing the internal structure, put the hat back on the virtual model. ## Hollow Area and Stock Price After reverse-activation, hide the virtual model. Let's do the internal stock structure first. In order not to affect our simulation speed, freeze all the panels that cannot be used. Before making the stock price, we usually have a hollow area behind the baseball cap. ### Digging the Hollow Area If we want to make the stock price, we need to dig out this hollow area before making the stock price. So we have to choose these two panels at the back. After canceling the link, set these two panels as symmetrical panels so that when we dig one side, the other side will automatically be symmetrical. ## Drawing the Reference If you want to have a reference, you can use the 3D panel tool in the 3D space to draw a reference first. First, untangle or activate the two panels at the back. Then we have to choose the 3D panel tool, click and draw the area we want to dig out. ### Adjusting the Panel After going to the panel line, double-click to end, then press Shift-A to display all virtual models.
